text: The pipeline begins with the data collection stage.
Raw wide dynamic range images are captured across varied artificial and natural lighting scenes.
The raw captures undergo postprocessing and formatting into lossless grayscale image files.
The dataset is then cleaned and classified, filtering out images with insufficient dynamic range.
Next, the tone mapping stage processes the qualified wide dynamic range images.
Only images with a dynamic range exceeding thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight are retained.
Twenty-five tone mapping operators are applied to compress the dynamic range for standard processing.
This conversion yields twenty-five distinct tone-mapped image sets ready for evaluation.
In the final phase, face detection models evaluate detection performance across each tone-mapped dataset.
Multiple standard face detectors are executed across all tone-mapped image variations.
Faces are detected under extreme lighting, challenging backlighting, and heavy shadow conditions.
Finally, detection outcomes are analyzed to assess the impact of different tone mapping techniques.
